prize_parts.citation: for developing the formal theory of how organised interests shape trade policy, making the political economy of protection analytically tractable and empirically testable

statement.case_for: I keep B001 as a single-part prize to Grossman and Helpman, with moderate confidence. The exchange changed one thing: the citation. In round 1 I added the trade-innovation-growth models. The shortlisted achievement is trade policy, special-interest politics and political-economy models of protection. Hjalmarsson and Friberg both pressed the point that the case must stand on the achievement actually listed, so I now word the citation around that achievement only. The core case is unchanged. Protection for sale put lobbying into an explicit equilibrium model in which a government trades off contributions against aggregate welfare. That produced a structural equation that empirical work could estimate. As a political scientist I note that measuring the influence of organised interests is hard, and the models gave researchers a precise object to measure. The attribution is a sustained two-person partnership, the work is about thirty years old and has been extended, taught and criticised throughout, and no colleague has raised a missing co-originator. The round-1 exchange did not show that B001 is the largest contribution on the list. It showed that the choice between B001 and B020 turns on how to weigh conceptual and organising influence against measurable consequences for data and estimation. I weigh the former somewhat higher, but not by a wide margin.
statement.case_against: The empirical record is the main weakness. Tests of the protection-for-sale predictions give mixed results that vary with specification and with how political contributions are measured. The case therefore rests on framework influence more than on settled confirmation. Mixed tests are partly a measurement problem, since lobbying data are poor, but I do not treat that as an excuse. B020 has the wider footprint in firm-level data, estimation and quantitative policy evaluation, and several colleagues who rank it first argue this persuasively. Helpman is credited in both B001 and B020, so the Committee must choose which strand it honours. The credit boundary on B020 is a real risk, but the empirical-footprint advantage is a real point in its favour. I have not found evidence in the openings that B001 has had large impact outside trade theory and political economy. My view is that its influence there is substantial, but that is from recollection and I have not verified it.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B020 first and B001 last. He argues that the protection-for-sale predictions have been confirmed less consistently than the selection and reallocation mechanisms, which have been checked against firm-level data in many countries. He says the absence of a trade prize since 2008 is a field argument and applies equally to B020.
responses.response: I agree on the 2008 point. My own round-1 argument was only that B001 is distinct from the 2008 recognition, and I give no weight to field balance as merit. I also accept that B020's mechanisms have been confirmed more consistently. We differ on what the mixed B001 record shows. A framework that yields a sharp, estimable prediction will produce varied estimates across specifications, and from recollection the early structural tests, such as Goldberg and Maggi (1999), came directly from the model. Contested magnitudes are different from no lasting contribution. I put this as a weighting difference, not a factual dispute. If the Committee weights empirical footprint above framework influence, as your ranking does, then B020 is the stronger candidate and I would accept it as a single-part award.

responses.point: Enflo ranks B020 first. She says cleaner credit does not make a contribution larger, that the 2008 point applies equally to both trade candidates, and that on the openings the firm-level framework contributed more than B001 does.
responses.response: I agree that cleaner credit is not a larger contribution, and I do not rely on it as a substitute for merit. It matters for a different reason. A prize with a clean attribution carries less risk of a priority dispute, and that is a legitimate consideration on its own terms. You and I agree that the Committee should recognise Helpman for only one strand. I read your argument as the strongest case against mine, because it rests on what each strand changed in practice. My answer is that protection for sale changed which questions can be posed about trade policy, and that the breadth of that influence is harder to measure than citation counts or data use. I accept that this is a harder case to document than yours.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B020 first. He argues that a theory whose influence runs ahead of its confirmation counts for less than a framework that went on to organise firm-level evidence. He says reasonable members can weigh theoretical depth against empirical traction differently.
responses.response: That is a fair statement of the real difference between us, and I accept it. I would add two qualifications. First, for B001 the lag between the theory and its confirmation is partly a data problem, since measuring political influence is harder than observing firm exports. Second, B001 did generate an empirical literature, even if its results are less uniform than B020's. I do not claim that settles the weighting. I would only ask that the Committee name the weighting explicitly, so that the choice between B001 and B020 does not turn on an unstated criterion.

responses.point: Hassler, the chair, ranks B016 first. He argues that the 2024 prize concerned the long-run historical origins of institutions, while B016 concerns how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity map into fiscal outcomes, and that the programme is broader than B001's single framework.
responses.response: Your distinction between historical origins and contemporary rules is sound, and it lowers my concern about overlap with the 2024 prize. I should say that I gave the 2024 presentation speech, so I am cautious about judging that overlap. Speeches given for the Academy do not show my own prize preference. My remaining concern about B016 is identification. The strongest cross-country constitutional results are still correlational in important respects. You argue that later within-country designs sharpened the programme, and I accept that. I still weigh the breadth of B016 against the sharper testability of the B001 models and keep B001 ahead. That is a close judgement. B016 is adjacent to my own field, which is another reason I do not list it among my alternatives.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B001 first. She says a framework can earn a prize through the questions it makes answerable, that mixed empirical results are normal for a testable model, and that the committee must decide which of Helpman's bodies of work it honours.
responses.response: I agree with most of this, and my round-1 reply supports it. Your argument has also moved me in one respect. You noted that the citation could become too broad if it covers lobbying and growth. For that reason I have dropped the trade-innovation-growth models from my citation. They are not part of the listed B001 achievement, and I do not want the case to rest on credit that is not in the ballot entry. I also take your point that B020 is the stronger candidate if the committee finds the mixed empirical record decisive. I put B020 first among my alternatives for that reason.

uncertainties: How much weight the Committee should give to the mixed empirical record of protection for sale against the framework's influence on research design. This weighting is the main difference between B001 and B020 and could reverse my ranking.
Whether the Committee will honour Helpman through B001 or B020. I would accept B020 as a single-part award if the Committee weights empirical footprint more heavily.
Whether B001's influence outside trade theory and political economy is large enough to meet the common criterion of broad impact. My view comes from recollection and I have not verified it.
Whether the B020 credit gap (Bernard, Eaton, Jensen, Kortum) is disqualifying. I cannot resolve it from the openings.
Whether the 2024 institutions prize should reduce the marginal case for B016. I have not weighed it as a decisive factor for or against any candidate.
I have not independently verified citations, priority claims or the empirical literature. My assessment rests on my recollection and on the colleagues' written positions.
statement.conflict_note: No collaboration with Grossman or Helpman (B001), or with the credited names on B020 or B019, appears in my supplied profile. Updated disclosure for B016, which is not in my configuration or alternatives: B016 is adjacent to my field of political institutions, democratisation and quality of government. My profile also lists a co-authored Governance paper on corruption as a collective-action problem with 'Persson' and Rothstein. The profile does not say which Persson. From recollection it is Anna Persson of Gothenburg and not Torsten Persson, who is credited on B016, but I have not verified this, so I disclose it without adjudicating it. I gave the 2024 presentation speech on institutions and prosperity, which does not establish a private prize preference. I am a Stockholm University colleague, in a different department, of members Hassler, Krusell and Boppart. I have no stated tie to any credited candidate on my preferred part.
